also: well, the last of the Romans!

evidence: Tac. Ann. 4.34: C. Cassium Rōmānōrum ultimum dīxisset
terms.comment: The historian Cremutius Cordus was put on trial for having praised Brutus and called Cassius “the last of the Romans”.
Traupman’s exclamation, with em, “there!”, and the words in the other order.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Tacitus, Annals 4.34, checked against the Latin Library texts (CLTK mirror) (12 November 2026).
